Hi! Both are hardware specific. Unsloth benched on b200's (cc 10.0), which takes the same dequantize path as 4090/3090/h100 - so their absolute numbers aren't universal either, just partial in the other direction. In fact, i tried couple days reproducing them and was so frustrated until i found out that they used 4xb200's (stated on their website). Still even with 4xb200's i couldn't reproduce their numbers, so I decided to make my own research and publish it openly for the community :)

Also, the chart itself is not really about absolute KLD, it's more like a lot of files measured on one machine. It was arduous but i wanted to be consistent and measured everything in isolation on 1 hardware. Wanted to use other servers with the "same" hardware, but it would insert noise into the results. So that's the whole reason i stopped reading published numbers - every publisher reports them from their own rig and dataset and nobody states which hardware, which dataset e.t.c.

I published all of it and reproduced my own results multiple times. On different server with similar hardware results are almost identical. I mean, if you choose the same gpus and just different cpus, motherboards e.t.c. But keep in mind that PCIe 5.0 16x with PCIe 4.0 2x can be deadly different :D

the hell is kl divergence ? if it's a probability , does 0.55 mean it's basically random ? Sorry I am not a math genius.

It is a measure of the similarity of the probability distributions of the next token between the original model and the quantized model in this case. No, I don't understand it either, but I know roughly that 0 means it is the same, and 1 means there is significant divergence. There is no upper limit to K-L divergence figure, for instance if quantized model shows high probability for original's low probability tokens and vice versa, it will go past 1. Task performance has been observed to drop if K-L divergence increases past 0.07, though this can be model-specific information.

Inference is partially random as token sampling is random, based on the probability distribution predicted by the model for the next token. As long as the model can recover from its own top token choices, even when they have been altered by quantization in its reasoning phase, there is little to no task degradation. To some degree, the inherent token sampling randomness hides the increased K-L divergence. But at some level of quantization, the model is too confused to fully recover, and that limit has been experimentally determined to occur around 0.07 K-L divergence according to ByteDance research.

Given that every GGUF besides the one that promotes even FP8 tensors to BF16 is past this limit, there is reasonable basis to make the claim that none of these 0731 models are the real deal except for the largest one which has to promote FP8 tensors to BF16 due to llama.cpp lacking support for this very important tensor format.

Someone appears to have called this line of reasoning "FP8-to-BF16 circlejerk". I implore one to reconsider words and the reasoning. We *know* that K-L divergence is correlated to task performance, we are just quibbling about the limit where it becomes observable. Our standardized AI tests are not very good at showing the difference, especially when it comes to extremely good models such as 0731. I am happily using this model at unsloth IQ3-XXS and it is way better than Qwen3.6-27B, so I am willing to eat the quality hit. But I also know that I don't get anywhere near the full capability of this model at the time being.

(Also, I am not rushing to download the AD-IQ2\_M model despite its shows slightly lower K-L divergence in test. These measurements are noisy and I am not convinced that points extremely close to each other are differentiated in any meaningful way by the K-L measure. All I care about is that we're fairly close to the best possible line.)
